sections.h2: Should a Lindenhurst, NY owner list, sell privately or sell for cash?
sections.html:
Any of the three can work, and all of them end at the same recording desk in Suffolk County. Nearly nine in ten Lindenhurst homes (87.6%) are lived in by their owners, so most sellers here are parting with a family house that has been theirs for years.

  • Broker listing: a good fit once the house shows well and you can ride out offers, inspections and mortgage approval.
  • Private sale: avoids a broker fee, though you screen buyers and run the contract steps with your attorney.
  • Cash sale: fits a house with repair needs, a rental permit gap, an estate to settle or a firm deadline, since the buyer accepts the property as it stands.

Price will move with condition under every option, so collect at least two opinions of value before deciding.

sections.h2: Where is Lindenhurst and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Lindenhurst is an incorporated village inside the Town of Babylon, on Long Island's South Shore with the Great South Bay along its southern edge. The village borders Copiague to the west, North Amityville to the northwest, North Lindenhurst to the north and West Babylon to the east. It covers about 3.75 square miles of land.

German settlers from Breslau gave the community its first name in 1873, and it was renamed Lindenhurst in 1891. Residents voted to incorporate as a village in 1923, and the village marked its centennial in 2023. Population jumped from 8,644 in 1950 to 20,905 in 1960 and peaked at 28,359 in 1970, so much of the housing dates from that postwar surge.

Water shapes the real estate here. In October 2012, Hurricane Sandy flooded more than half of the village's streets, with water up to about 6 feet south of Montauk Highway. Buyers who ask about flood history on the south side of the village are asking a fair question, so gather your elevation, insurance and repair records before showings or an offer review.

sections.h2: What village services and amenities come with a Lindenhurst address?
sections.html:
A Lindenhurst address brings village-run services that a buyer will ask about, and the village website lists most of them in one place. The village runs its own Building Department, Code Enforcement, Public Works for highway and sanitation, a Parks Department and a Village Court. A posted sanitation calendar covers pickup days.

  • A village marina with dock space, and Irmisch Park along the water.
  • The Village Museum and a Historical Society, tied to the Breslau history.
  • A youth center, youth leagues and a summer recreation program.
  • A Business Improvement District and a village fire department.

Homes with a second unit fall under the village's Two-Family Review Board and a two-family page in the Building Department. If your house has an accessory apartment, ask the department how it is classified before you list. Montauk Highway also runs through the village.

sections.h2: What rules apply if I rent out my Lindenhurst house before selling?
sections.html:
Lindenhurst requires a rental permit, and the village's rental permit page says a first-time application must be notarized and is followed by an inspection. Permits must be renewed every two years unless the permit says otherwise, and renewal also triggers an inspection.

Inspections are booked with the Building Department, which lists set weekday windows on Tuesdays and Wednesdays for residential rentals and a separate schedule for mixed-use rentals. If you are a landlord preparing to sell, check that the permit on file matches how the house is actually used. Before a contract is signed, ask the department what it holds on your address.

sections.h2: How do Lindenhurst property taxes and grievances work?
sections.html:
Lindenhurst homeowners get several tax bills, because the village taxes separately from the Town of Babylon and the school district. The village bill is a once-a-year tax that is mailed by March 1 and due April 1, and the village Tax Department accepts it only in full. A payment received after April 1 draws a 5 percent penalty plus a $2.00 fee, and the charge keeps growing monthly.

The village Assessment Department prepares the roll for almost 10,000 parcels and handles exemptions for senior citizens, veterans, firefighters and volunteer ambulance workers, non-profit organizations and clergy. Those exemptions reduce only the village tax bill. Senior applications require income of no more than $37,400, are renewed every year, and are due by October 1.

  • Village grievance: the window opens each November 1 and closes on Grievance Day, the third Tuesday of November, which is November 17 this year.
  • Town of Babylon grievance: filed with the Town Assessor, due by the third Tuesday in May, with forms available from mid-April. The 2026 period has ended.
  • Small claims: if the Town's Board of Assessment Review denies a grievance, a small claims petition goes to the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead.

Tell the village Assessment Department when ownership changes or a mortgage is satisfied, so the next bill goes to the right party. Tax information is not given out by phone, so request a tax search by email using the village's request form.

sections.h2: What will recording a Lindenhurst deed run in Suffolk County?
sections.html:
Suffolk County's deed fee schedule computes transfer tax at $2.00 per $500 of consideration or any fraction of it, and its own example turns $750 into $4.00. A sale at the village's $521,500 typical value would owe about $2,088. The Clerk's schedule lists recording fees of $245 plus $5.00 per page, in a version revised July 17, 2024, so confirm current numbers before you budget.

When a residential price reaches $1,000,000 a 1% mansion tax is also due from the buyer, paid in cash or by certified check made out to the Suffolk County Clerk. The tax map number you need for the forms comes from the Town Assessor, which for Lindenhurst is the Town of Babylon's office in Town Hall on East Sunrise Highway.

Under the state's transfer tax guidance, the base tax falls on the seller, with the contract able to shift it. After closing, close out your STAR registration, which the STAR page asks owners to do on a sale.

faqs.q: Which district runs the schools in Lindenhurst?
faqs.a: The Lindenhurst Union Free School District serves all of the village, plus most of North Lindenhurst and a small part of West Babylon. The district runs six elementary schools, one middle school and one high school.

faqs.q: What is the due date for the Lindenhurst village tax?
faqs.a: Village tax is due April 1, and bills go out by March 1. It is a once-a-year tax, payment is accepted only in full, and a late payment adds 5 percent and a $2.00 fee.

faqs.q: What are the Lindenhurst grievance dates?
faqs.a: The village's Grievance Day lands on the third Tuesday of November, which is November 17 in 2026. The Town of Babylon runs its own process, ending on the third Tuesday of May.

faqs.q: Is a rental permit needed for a Lindenhurst rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Lindenhurst requires a rental permit with a notarized first application and an inspection, and permits are renewed every two years. Ask the village Building Department about mixed-use properties, which have their own inspection hours.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for transfer tax on a Lindenhurst sale?
faqs.a: The seller carries the state's $2.00-per-$500 tax by default, though the contract can move it. A buyer pays the separate 1% mansion tax once a residential price hits $1,000,000.
